MeitY Unveils DEPA for AI Training, a ‘Sealed Room’ Framework to Train AI on Sensitive Data Without Exposing It
By Elets News Network - 31 October 2026

Share:

India has some of the richest datasets in the world, from hospital scans to bank transaction histories, but almost none of it reaches the teams building AI models. Hospitals and banks rarely share it: they earn little from doing so and face penalties of up to ₹250 crore under the data protection law if it leaks. The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) now wants to break that stalemate by sending AI models to the data instead of sending data to the developers.

MeitY Secretary S Krishnan unveiled the Data Empowerment and Protection Architecture (DEPA) for AI Training handbook at a roundtable in Bengaluru on 30 October. The draft framework, prepared with the volunteer-led think tank iSPIRT Foundation, is pitched as India’s digital public infrastructure for AI, and says it has the potential to unlock $500 billion in AI-driven value for India’s GDP by 2030.

Breaking the “data deadlock”

The handbook calls the core problem a “data deadlock”: the data needed to solve the next generation of problems is split across domains and locked behind separate institutional and regulatory walls. It argues that simply stripping out names and ID numbers is not enough, because anonymised data can often be re-identified and loses much of its usefulness along the way.

DEPA itself is not new. NITI Aayog introduced it in 2020

Vyoma.AI, Larsen & Toubro’s (L&T) AI cloud and data centre business, has broken ground on a 52 MW AI-ready data centre in Chennai as it expands its infrastructure to support AI workloads and cloud computing.

MeitY Unveils DEPA for AI Training, a ‘Sealed Room’ Framework to Train AI on Sensitive Data Without Exposing It
By Elets News Network - 31 October 2026

Share:

India has some of the richest datasets in the world, from hospital scans to bank transaction histories, but almost none of it reaches the teams building AI models. Hospitals and banks rarely share it: they earn little from doing so and face penalties of up to ₹250 crore under the data protection law if it leaks. The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) now wants to break that stalemate by sending AI models to the data instead of sending data to the developers.

MeitY Secretary S Krishnan unveiled the Data Empowerment and Protection Architecture (DEPA) for AI Training handbook at a roundtable in Bengaluru on 30 October. The draft framework, prepared with the volunteer-led think tank iSPIRT Foundation, is pitched as India’s digital public infrastructure for AI, and says it has the potential to unlock $500 billion in AI-driven value for India’s GDP by 2030.

Breaking the “data deadlock”

The handbook calls the core problem a “data deadlock”: the data needed to solve the next generation of problems is split across domains and locked behind separate institutional and regulatory walls. It argues that simply stripping out names and ID numbers is not enough, because anonymised data can often be re-identified and loses much of its usefulness along the way.

DEPA itself is not new. NITI Aayog introduced it in 2020

MeitY Unveils DEPA for AI Training, a ‘Sealed Room’ Framework to Train AI on Sensitive Data Without Exposing It
By Elets News Network - 31 October 2026

Share:

India has some of the richest datasets in the world, from hospital scans to bank transaction histories, but almost none of it reaches the teams building AI models. Hospitals and banks rarely share it: they earn little from doing so and face penalties of up to ₹250 crore under the data protection law if it leaks. The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) now wants to break that stalemate by sending AI models to the data instead of sending data to the developers.

MeitY Secretary S Krishnan unveiled the Data Empowerment and Protection Architecture (DEPA) for AI Training handbook at a roundtable in Bengaluru on 30 October. The draft framework, prepared with the volunteer-led think tank iSPIRT Foundation, is pitched as India’s digital public infrastructure for AI, and says it has the potential to unlock $500 billion in AI-driven value for India’s GDP by 2030.

Breaking the “data deadlock”

The handbook calls the core problem a “data deadlock”: the data needed to solve the next generation of problems is split across domains and locked behind separate institutional and regulatory walls. It argues that simply stripping out names and ID numbers is not enough, because anonymised data can often be re-identified and loses much of its usefulness along the way.

DEPA itself is not new. NITI Aayog introduced it in 2020
